title: Contribution syllabus and component sunset checklist
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a concise, developer-friendly contribution syllabus and a deterministic sunset checklist for components (tokens, buttons, tables, charts). The goal is to reduce review friction, make RFC gating repeatable, and give product teams a predictable migration path when items are deprecated. Deliverables: a one-page syllabus for new contributors, an expanded review checklist for PRs, an RFC gating rubric, and a compact sunset checklist with migration examples for tokens and charts.
acceptance_criteria: One-page contributor syllabus published in Confluence with links to PR template and lint rules
Review checklist added to the design repo as a markdown file and referenced in PR templates
RFC gating rubric defined with explicit pass/fail criteria for compatibility, accessibility, performance, and telemetry
Sunset checklist for components documented with at least two migration examples (tokens -> aliasing, chart v2 -> v3 mapping)
At least one design-engineering pairing session scheduled to onboard the first external contributor using the syllabus
steps: Draft contributor syllabus (1 page) that covers: scope of contributions, required docs, PR labels, owner rotation, and who to ping for approvals
Create REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md in design repo and link it from PR template
Define RFC gating rubric and circulate to PM and Eng for +1s
Compile sunset checklist with phases: announce, soft-deprecate (alias), hard-deprecate (remove), and monitoring windows
Add token migration example mapping old tokens to aliases with a codemod suggestion
Draft chart migration guide that lists breaking props and recommended adapters
Run a dry run: apply syllabus to an internal small change (icon button spacing) and collect feedback
Ship docs and update the design onboarding checklist in Confluence
review_checklist: Purpose: Why is this change needed? Link to ticket and user story
Design files: include Figma link with component variants and tokens used
Accessibility: keyboard nav, color contrast, ARIA where applicable
Telemetry: is there a metric to track after rollout? Add tracking ticket if needed
Performance: note expected render/paint changes; include microbench if component affects large lists
API stability: are props backwards-compatible? If not, explain migration plan
Token usage: prefer aliases over direct token deletion; add mapping table
Docs: update component docs, examples, and migration notes
Ownership: list primary and secondary owners and rotation schedule
Testing: unit/visual/regression tests included; provide Percy/Chromatic links
Rollout plan: canary percentage, fallback, and rollback criteria
rfc_lifecycle: Intake: submit RFC draft to design/rfc folder with problem statement and non-goals
Review window: 7 calendar days for initial feedback from Design/Eng/PM
Gating rubric: must meet >=4 of 5 categories (compatibility, accessibility, performance, telemetry, operational cost) with no 'hard fails'
Approval: design lead + eng tech lead + one PM sign-off required for planned acceptance
Post-acceptance: assign implementation owner, schedule rollout cadence, and create sunset ticket if the RFC replaces existing behavior
Change window: any breaking changes must include a 90-day soft-deprecation period with automated aliasing where possible
deprecation_policy_summary: Announcement: 2-week heads-up in both Design Channel and the Release Notes with migration guidance
Soft-deprecate: introduce aliases and warnings in console/docs; keep old API for min(90 days, customer-agreed SLA)
Hard-deprecate: remove the old API after the window; ship migration codemod and samples
Exceptions: security or urgent performance issues can shorten deprecation windows after Exec approval
Customer impact categories: none, low, medium, high — deprecation window scales with impact
Compliance: for Private customers, notify account owners and offer upgrade assist sessions
migration_guides: Token aliasing example: OLD_TOKEN_BORDER -> alias: REDWOOD-BORDER/neutral-200; sample codemod: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-migrations/pull/274
Chart migration: v2 stacked axis-> v3 separate scale API; sample adapter in repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/chart-adapters/tree/main/v2-to-v3
Button spacing: recommended token migration and fallback CSS variable strategy (example snippet in Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DS/Button+Spacing+Migration
Tables: row-height and cell-padding changes documented with accessibility rationale and compatibility helpers
decisions: Keep 90-day baseline soft-deprecation window for non-critical items
Require telemetry or sampling plan for any change that touches >10% of API surface
Adopt alias-first strategy for tokens to minimize breakage
Create a single REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md to centralize review criteria rather than scattered docs
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: contributors skip checklist -> Mitigation: enforce checklist via PR template and bot comment reminders
Risk: silent breakage for Private deployments -> Mitigation: account notification step and optional migration support
Risk: too many deprecations back-to-back -> Mitigation: release cadence limit and cross-team calendar coordination
Risk: ambiguous ownership -> Mitigation: require primary and secondary owners on every PR and RFC
